children: , the largest U.S. bank by assets, climbed approximately 0.5% to $355.01 Wednesday as it pushed its corporate-banking franchise into Greece. The new operation will bring lending, financing, hedging and investment-banking services to large and midsized Greek companies.

The bank has expanded staffing across its Europe, Middle East and Africa global corporate bank by roughly 25% over the past two years. Greece gives JPMorgan another gateway for connecting local companies with its global payments and capital-markets machinery. Management did not disclose a revenue target or planned headcount for the country.

JPMorgan generated $58 billion in managed second-quarter revenue and $21.2 billion in net income, while overseeing approximately $5 trillion in assets. Greece is too small to transform those numbers overnight, but it can strengthen cross-border relationships without forcing the bank to recreate its product engine. The picture adds a valuation warning: the $355.01 share price sits 12.24% above the $316.30 GF Value estimate, suggesting investors already pay a premium for JPMorgan's scale and execution.

title: JPMorgan Gains as Its European Hiring Offensive Reaches Greece
